options.text: Resistance increases as current increases
The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, provided the temperature remains constant
Voltage equals current plus resistance
Current is directly proportional to resistance at constant temperature

questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, provided physical conditions such as temperature remain constant.

questions.stem: Which I-V graph represents an ohmic conductor?

options.text: A straight line through the origin
A curve that bends upwards
A curve that only exists in the positive quadrant
A horizontal line

questions.explanation: An ohmic conductor has a straight-line I-V graph passing through the origin, showing that current is directly proportional to voltage with constant resistance.

questions.stem: Why does a filament lamp NOT obey Ohm's law?

options.text: Because it only works with alternating current
Because the voltage across it is always constant
Because its resistance is always zero
Because as the current increases, the filament heats up, increasing its resistance

questions.explanation: As current flows through a filament lamp, the filament heats up. This increases the resistance, so the I-V graph curves rather than being a straight line, meaning it does not obey Ohm's law.

questions.stem: What is the key characteristic of a diode?

options.text: It only allows current to flow in one direction (forward bias)
It has constant resistance in both directions
Its resistance decreases when it gets hot
It stores electrical charge

questions.explanation: A diode allows current to flow in one direction only (forward bias) and has very high resistance in the reverse direction. Its I-V characteristic shows current only in the forward direction above a threshold voltage.

questions.stem: How does the resistance of a thermistor (NTC type) change as its temperature increases?

options.text: Its resistance stays the same
Its resistance increases
Its resistance first increases then decreases
Its resistance decreases

questions.explanation: An NTC (negative temperature coefficient) thermistor has a resistance that decreases as temperature increases. This makes it useful as a temperature sensor in circuits.

questions.stem: How does the resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR) change as light intensity increases?

options.text: Its resistance increases
Its resistance decreases
Its resistance stays the same
Its resistance drops to zero

questions.explanation: An LDR has a high resistance in the dark and a low resistance in bright light. As light intensity increases, more charge carriers are released, decreasing its resistance.

questions.stem: In a voltage divider circuit, what happens to the output voltage across a thermistor as the temperature increases?

options.text: The output voltage decreases because the thermistor's resistance decreases
The output voltage increases because the thermistor's resistance increases
The output voltage becomes zero
The output voltage stays the same

questions.explanation: As temperature increases, the NTC thermistor's resistance decreases. In a voltage divider, the voltage is shared in proportion to resistance, so the voltage across the thermistor decreases as its resistance decreases.
